3:1.sourceText: Διὸ μηκέτι στέγοντες ηὐδοκήσαμεν καταλειφθῆναι ἐν Ἀθήναις μόνοι,
3:1.targetText: И потому, не терпя более, мы восхотели остаться в Афинах одни

groups.note: The actual first-person plural willing predicate supplies the overt Russian subject.

unmappedTarget.reason: Russian opens with an additional additive. Actual διό is the inference connector.

3:2.sourceText: καὶ ἐπέμψαμεν Τιμόθεον, τὸν ἀδελφὸν ἡμῶν καὶ διάκονον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, εἰς τὸ στηρίξαι ὑμᾶς καὶ παρακαλέσαι ὑπὲρ τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν
3:2.targetText: и послали Тимофея, брата нашего и служителя Божия и сотрудника нашего в благовествовании Христовом, чтобы утвердить вас и утешить в вере вашей,

groups.note: The actual preposition and article introduce the coordinated infinitives. Russian expresses a purpose conjunction.
Actual N1904 uses ὑπέρ with faith where the printed TR has περί. The actual preposition can express the respect or concern of encouragement, expressed by Russian в.

unmappedSource.reason: These printed Greek articles are unexpressed in the local Russian noun, modifier or infinitive phrases.

unmappedTarget.reason: Printed TR includes this distinct title and possessive. Actual N1904 prints brother and minister; the additional conjunction, title and possessive remain separate.

3:3.sourceText: τὸ μηδένα σαίνεσθαι ἐν ταῖς θλίψεσιν ταύταις. αὐτοὶ γὰρ οἴδατε ὅτι εἰς τοῦτο κείμεθα·
3:3.targetText: чтобы никто не поколебался в скорбях сих: ибо вы сами знаете, что так нам суждено.

groups.note: The actual accusative neuter article introduces the infinitival clause. The printed TR has the dative form τῷ.
Actual σαίνω in this passive infinitive means being unsettled. Russian uses an intransitive finite form for the same affected participant.
The actual negative adjective in the subject position supplies the Russian negative pronoun and agreeing verbal negative.
The actual emphatic personal pronoun refers to the addressed knowers. Russian expresses both subject and emphasis.
The actual first-person plural verb of being set is expressed impersonally with the same participants in the Russian dative.
The actual destination expression to this is rendered as the manner of being destined in Russian.

studyHeads.note: Open the actual demonstrative in the joint prepositional relation.

unmappedSource.reason: These printed Greek articles are unexpressed in the local Russian noun, modifier or infinitive phrases.

3:4.sourceText: καὶ γὰρ ὅτε πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἦμεν, προελέγομεν ὑμῖν ὅτι μέλλομεν θλίβεσθαι, καθὼς καὶ ἐγένετο καὶ οἴδατε.
3:4.targetText: Ибо мы и тогда, как были у вас, предсказывали вам, что будем страдать, как и случилось, и вы знаете.

groups.note: The actual temporal conjunction is expanded with a Russian correlative.
The first-person plural predicting predicate provides the overt Russian speaker.
The second-person plural knowing predicate provides the overt Russian subject.

3:5.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο κἀγὼ μηκέτι στέγων ἔπεμψα εἰς τὸ γνῶναι τὴν πίστιν ὑμῶν, μή πως ἐπείρασεν ὑμᾶς ὁ πειράζων καὶ εἰς κενὸν γένηται ὁ κόπος ἡμῶν.
3:5.targetText: Посему и я, не терпя более, послал узнать о вере вашей, чтобы как не искусил вас искуситель и не сделался тщетным труд наш.

groups.note: The actual preposition with the demonstrative gives the one Russian causal connector.
The actual written crasis combines the additive particle and first-person singular pronoun.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual knowing infinitive has the purpose preposition and article. Russian gives it directly after sending.
The actual result predicate has a preposition. Russian uses a predicate adjective in the instrumental.
These printed Greek articles are unexpressed in the local Russian noun, modifier or infinitive phrases.

unmappedTarget.reason: The actual knowing verb takes a direct object. Russian makes the topic overt.
Russian gives the later apprehension clause an overt conjunction. Actual Greek gives the negative with the indefinite manner word.
Russian repeats the negative in the second apprehension clause. Actual Greek has one initial negative expression.

3:6.sourceText: Ἄρτι δὲ ἐλθόντος Τιμοθέου πρὸς ἡμᾶς ἀφ’ ὑμῶν καὶ εὐαγγελισαμένου ἡμῖν τὴν πίστιν καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην ὑμῶν, καὶ ὅτι ἔχετε μνείαν ἡμῶν ἀγαθὴν πάντοτε, ἐπιποθοῦντες ἡμᾶς ἰδεῖν καθάπερ καὶ ἡμεῖς ὑμᾶς,
3:6.targetText: Теперь же, когда пришел к нам от вас Тимофей и принес нам добрую весть о вере и любви вашей и что вы всегда имеете добрую память о нас, желая нас видеть, как и мы вас,

groups.note: The actual good-news verb supplies the Russian report phrase. The later actual good adjective belongs to memory.
The actual second-person finite having verb supplies the overt Russian subject.

unmappedSource.reason: These printed Greek articles are unexpressed in the local Russian noun, modifier or infinitive phrases.

unmappedTarget.reason: Russian turns the actual temporal genitive absolute into a finite clause with a conjunction.
Russian gives the topic of the good news with a preposition. Actual Greek has the direct object nouns.
Russian expresses the person remembered in a prepositional phrase. Actual Greek has the genitive.

3:7.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο παρεκλήθημεν, ἀδελφοί, ἐφ’ ὑμῖν ἐπὶ πάσῃ τῇ ἀνάγκῃ καὶ θλίψει ἡμῶν διὰ τῆς ὑμῶν πίστεως,
3:7.targetText: то мы, при всей скорби и нужде нашей, утешились вами, братия, ради вашей веры;

groups.note: The Greek causal relationship answers the preceding arrival and report. Russian expresses the relationship with its temporal correlative.

studyHeads.note: Open the actual demonstrative in the joint causal expression.

groups.note: The actual first-person plural passive remains the same affected party in the Russian reflexive-form expression. The overt subject comes from the actual personal ending.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual Greek introduces the cause or occasion with ἐπί plus dative. Russian gives the associated person as instrumental вами.
These printed Greek articles are unexpressed in the local Russian noun, modifier or infinitive phrases.

3:8.sourceText: ὅτι νῦν ζῶμεν ἐὰν ὑμεῖς στήκετε ἐν Κυρίῳ.
3:8.targetText: ибо теперь мы живы, когда вы стоите в Господе.

groups.note: The actual first-person plural live verb is expressed by a Russian adjective with the same overt subject.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual ἐάν introduces a conditional standing clause. Russian expresses that subordinate clause with a temporal connector.

unmappedTarget.reason: Russian marks the clause as temporal. Both compared Greek printings use the conditional connector ἐάν.

3:9.sourceText: τίνα γὰρ εὐχαριστίαν δυνάμεθα τῷ Θεῷ ἀνταποδοῦναι περὶ ὑμῶν ἐπὶ πάσῃ τῇ χαρᾷ ᾗ χαίρομεν δι’ ὑμᾶς ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν,
3:9.targetText: Какую благодарность можем мы воздать Богу за вас, за всю радость, которою радуемся о вас пред Богом нашим,

groups.note: The actual first-person plural ability predicate supplies the Russian pronoun.

unmappedSource.reason: The written explanatory connector is implicit in Russian.
These printed Greek articles are unexpressed in the local Russian noun, modifier or infinitive phrases.

3:10.sourceText: νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ὑπερεκπερισσοῦ δεόμενοι εἰς τὸ ἰδεῖν ὑμῶν τὸ πρόσωπον καὶ καταρτίσαι τὰ ὑστερήματα τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν;
3:10.targetText: ночь и день всеусердно молясь о том, чтобы видеть лице ваше и дополнить, чего недоставало вере вашей?

groups.note: The actual single intensive adverb expresses earnestness. The full printed TR has two written words ὑπὲρ ἐκπερισσοῦ.
Actual preposition and article introduce the coordinated infinitives. Russian uses a correlative and purpose connector.

studyHeads.note: Open the actual preposition in the purpose frame.

3:11.sourceText: Αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ Θεὸς καὶ Πατὴρ ἡμῶν καὶ ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς κατευθύναι τὴν ὁδὸν ἡμῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς·
3:11.targetText: Сам же Бог и Отец наш и Господь наш Иисус Христос да управит путь наш к вам.

groups.note: The actual aorist optative gives the wish expressed by Russian particle and finite verb.

unmappedSource.reason: These printed Greek articles are unexpressed in the local Russian noun, modifier or infinitive phrases.

unmappedTarget.reason: Printed TR adds Christ after Jesus. Actual N1904 has Jesus alone here.

3:12.sourceText: ὑμᾶς δὲ ὁ Κύριος πλεονάσαι καὶ περισσεύσαι τῇ ἀγάπῃ εἰς ἀλλήλους καὶ εἰς πάντας, καθάπερ καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς ὑμᾶς,
3:12.targetText: А вас Господь да исполнит и преисполнит любовью друг к другу и ко всем, какою мы исполнены к вам,

groups.note: The first actual causative increase verb in the optative is expressed as fill with a Russian wish particle.

These printed Greek articles are unexpressed in the local Russian noun, modifier or infinitive phrases.

3:13.sourceText: εἰς τὸ στηρίξαι ὑμῶν τὰς καρδίας ἀμέμπτους ἐν ἁγιωσύνῃ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς ἡμῶν ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ μετὰ πάντων τῶν ἁγίων αὐτοῦ.
3:13.targetText: чтобы утвердить сердца ваши непорочными во святыне пред Богом и Отцем нашим в пришествие Господа нашего Иисуса Христа со всеми святыми Его. Аминь.

groups.note: The actual preposition and article introduce an infinitive of purpose or result, expressed by a Russian conjunction.
